s.d: pertaining to being cursed
s.g: cursed; accursed
s.c: The occurrences of ἐπάρατος in ⟦John 7:49|John 7:49⟧ and ἐπικατάρατος in ⟦Galatians 3:10|Galatians 3:10⟧ imply much more than being cursed by some person. In such contexts, the real meaning is that these individuals have already been condemned by God or are under the threat of such a condemnation.

s.d: pertaining to being cursed
s.g: cursed; accursed
s.c: The occurrences of ἐπάρατος in ⟦John 7:49|John 7:49⟧ and ἐπικατάρατος in ⟦Galatians 3:10|Galatians 3:10⟧ imply much more than being cursed by some person. In such contexts, the real meaning is that these individuals have already been condemned by God or are under the threat of such a condemnation.

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: a day immediately following a previous day{N:001}
s.g: the next day; on the next day

s.d: to happen to someone or something, with the implication of an event which is undesirable
s.g: to happen to; to come upon; to overtake

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move to or on to, generally with the implication of having arrived
s.g: to come to; to arrive
s.c: In the rendering of ⟦Luke 1:35|Luke 1:35⟧ it is important to avoid the kind of literal translation which might suggest sexual relations.

s.d: to use sudden physical force against someone as the outgrowth of a hostile attitude
s.g: to attack; to assault
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to attack’ is simply ‘to start fighting against.’ In some languages, however, the equivalent is ‘to jump on’ or ‘to grab to do harm to.’

s.d: to happen to someone or something, with the implication of an event which is undesirable
s.g: to happen to; to come upon; to overtake

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Beyond, On the Other Side Of
s.d: a position farther away than a reference point
s.g: beyond; farther away

s.d: to reach out or stretch out toward some goal
s.g: to reach out; to stretch toward
s.c: In ⟦Philippians 3:13|Philippians 3:13⟧ ἐπεκτείνομαι is used figuratively to suggest intense effort as well as firm purpose.

s.d: to attempt energetically to attain a state or condition
s.g: to seek strongly to; to try hard to

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: any type of outer garment{N:001}
s.g: cloak; coat; robe
s.c: The choice of an equivalent for these terms relating to ‘outer garments’ will depend largely upon the specific context and the usage in each receptor language. The most common equivalent is a term meaning ‘coat.’

s.d: to put a garment on over existing clothing
s.g: to put on over; to put on an additional garment

s.d: to ask for information{N:001}
s.g: to ask; to ask a question
s.c: In a number of languages a term such as ἐρωτάω or ἐπερωτάω implies an introduction of direct discourse, so that in ⟦Luke 9:45|Luke 9:45⟧, for example, it may be necessary to translate ‘they were afraid to ask him, What do you mean by what you said?’

s.d: to ask for, usually with the implication of an underlying question{N:002}
s.g: to ask for; to request

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judicial Hearing, Inquiry
s.d: to attempt in a legal or semi-legal procedure to know the truth about a matter, normally by interrogation
s.g: to question; to interrogate; to try to learn

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπερωτάω<SDBG:ἐπερωτάω:000001>}[b] ‘to ask for,’ {D:33.161}) that which is asked for
s.g: request; appeal
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἐπερώτημα in ⟦1 Peter 3:21|1 Peter 3:21⟧ as meaning ‘pledge’ or ‘promise,’ in which case it may be classified under LN 33.288. Accordingly, the phrase συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς θεόν may be rendered as ‘a promise made to God from a good conscience.’

s.dp: Learn › Be Ready To Learn, Pay Attention
s.d: to be in a continuous state of readiness to learn of any future danger, need, or error, and to respond appropriately
s.g: to pay attention to; to keep on the lookout for; to be alert for; to be on one’s guard against

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: to hold firmly to a particular belief
s.g: to hold firmly to; to continue to believe
s.c: The equivalent of ἐπέχω and προσέχω may be simply ‘to continue to strongly believe’ or ‘to not give up at all to believe.’|It is also possible to understand ἐπέχω in ⟦Philippians 2:16|Philippians 2:16⟧ as meaning ‘to offer.’

s.d: to direct one’s attention to a particular object or event
s.g: to notice; to watch

s.d: to stay or remain in a place beyond some point of time
s.g: to stay on; to remain

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Treat Badly
s.d: to mistreat, with the implication of threats and abuse
s.g: to mistreat

s.dp: Spacial Positions › On, Upon, On the Surface Of
s.d: a position on a surface of an object, whether vertical or horizontal, and in contact with the object
s.g: on; upon

s.dp: Spacial Positions › At, Beside, Near, Far
s.d: a position in proximity to or in the immediate vicinity of an object or other position
s.g: at; by

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position within an area determined by other objects and distributed among such objects{N:001}
s.g: among; with

s.dp: Spacial Positions › In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
s.d: a position before, with the implication of a relationship of authority
s.g: before

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension toward a goal, usually implying reaching the goal{N:002}
s.g: to; toward; in the direction of

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension to a goal, with implied contact on a horizontal surface
s.g: on; onto

s.d: (with the accusative) a marker of the one upon whom responsibility falls
s.g: on; upon
s.c: See also LN 37.102.

s.d: a marker of the experiencer, often with the implication of an action by a superior force or agency
s.g: to; at; on

s.d: (with the dative) a marker of instrument as the basis for some event
s.g: by; by means of

s.d: (with the accusative or dative) a marker of opposition in a judicial or quasijudicial context
s.g: against

s.d: (with the dative) a marker of persons benefited by an event, with the implication of their being in a dependent relationship
s.g: for

s.d: a marker of an addition to what already exists, but with the possible implication of something more significant
s.g: in addition to; and

s.d: a marker of the object over which someone exercises a control or authority
s.g: over; with responsibility for

s.d: a marker of cause or reason as the basis for a subsequent event or state
s.g: because of; on the basis of

s.d: a marker of purpose, pointing to the goal of an event or state
s.g: for the purpose of; for the sake of; in order to

s.d: (with the genitive) a marker of content as a means of specifying a particular referent
s.g: concerning; with respect to; with reference to; about; in

s.d: a marker of the basis of some event
s.g: on the basis of; in view of

s.dp: Degree › Up To, As Much As, To the Degree That [Marked Extent of Degree]
s.d: a degree extending to a particular point as marked by the context
s.g: to the point of; to the extent of; to the degree that; up to
s.c: See also ⟦Romans 11:13|Romans 11:13⟧ in LN 78.52.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a marker of a point of time which is simultaneous to or overlaps with another point of time{N:003}
s.g: when; at the time of

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: a marker of the extent of time within a unit
s.g: during; in the course of; within; for

s.dp: Case › Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
s.d: (with the accusative) a marker of agent, with the added implication of effect upon the agent
s.g: by
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦2 Thessalonians 1:10|2 Thessalonians 1:10⟧ there is a double relation marked by ἐπί, for it may be construed as marking the affected participant with τὸ μαρτύριον and at the same time the agent participant with ἐπιστεύθη. It is this double role which may account for the use of ἐπί rather than ὑπό, which would clearly mark a relation with ἐπιστεύθη, or πρός, which would indicate clearly a relation with μαρτύριον.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: (an idiom, literally: at the doors) a point of time subsequent to another point of time and indicating imminence, that is to say, the subsequent event is regarded as almost begun
s.g: soon; very soon

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time
s.g: long; long time; for some time

s.dp: Control, Rule › Assign to a Role or Function
s.d: (an idiom, literally: upon someone’s head) to accept responsibility for some action, often with the implication of blame
s.g: upon someone’s head; responsibility
s.c: This statement in ⟦Acts 18:6|Acts 18:6⟧ is no doubt an adage meaning that anything bad which may happen to a person, including one’s death, will be one’s own responsibility, and therefore no one else is to blame.|It is also possible to classify this idiom in Domain 90D. Note that in LN 37.102 the focus is on the assignment of responsibility.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to sit upon the seat of Moses) to have the capacity to interpret the Law of Moses with authority{N:004}
s.g: to be an authority concerning the Law of Moses

s.d: (an idiom, literally: on the housetops) pertaining to being widely known in view of the events in question having taken place in public{N:005}
s.g: in public; publicly

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: (an idiom, literally: upon enough) duration of time for a considerable period, with the focus upon sufficiency of time
s.g: during a considerable period of time; for a long time

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move to or on to, generally with the implication of having arrived
s.g: to come to; to arrive

s.d: to move up onto some object
s.g: to embark; to go onto; to mount
s.c: In a high percentage of languages it is necessary to use quite distinct terms in speaking of boarding a ship in contrast with mounting a donkey. A wrong choice in such a context can be seriously misleading.

s.d: to throw something on{N:001}
s.g: to throw on

s.d: to place something on something
s.g: to put on; to place on; to lay on

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: to strike upon and into (with special reference to the action of waves)
s.g: to splash into

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: to belong to or to come to belong to, with the possible implication of by right or by inheritance
s.g: to belong to

s.d: to give careful consideration to various implications of an issue
s.g: to reflect on; to think about seriously; to think deeply about
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπιβάλλω in ⟦Mark 14:72|Mark 14:72⟧, see LN 68.5.

s.d: to begin an activity, with special emphasis upon the inception or possibly the suddenness with which the event takes place
s.g: to begin
s.c: It would also be possible to understand ἐπιβάλλω in ⟦Mark 14:72|Mark 14:72⟧ as meaning ‘when he thought of it’ or ‘when he reflected on it’ (see LN 30.7).

s.dp: Control, Rule › Seize, Take into Custody
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to lay hands on) to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity
s.g: to seize; to arrest

s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back) to begin some activity requiring close attention but then to change one’s mind about proceeding
s.g: to start to do something and then to hesitate; to begin but have second thoughts about continuing
s.c: It is probably best to regard the phrase ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ᾽ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω as a part of a traditional saying referring to anyone who has second thoughts about undertaking some new or different enterprise, but the particular manner in which this is adapted to a statement concerning ‘the kingdom of God’ makes its strictly idiomatic structure somewhat doubtful.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be a Financial Burden
s.d: to be a financial burden to someone by requiring too much support
s.g: to burden; to be a financial burden to

s.d: to cause to mount, as in the case of an animal
s.g: to cause to mount
s.c: In ⟦Luke 10:34|Luke 10:34⟧ it is difficult to know whether the causative aspect of the verb includes ‘helping him get on’ or ‘having him get on.’

s.d: to notice and pay special attention to{N:001}
s.g: to notice especially
s.c: In the case of ἐπιβλέπω in ⟦James 2:3|James 2:3⟧, there is obviously a considerable measure of cognitive involvement, for not only sight but evaluation is also involved. For another interpretation of ἐπιβλέπω in ⟦James 2:3|James 2:3⟧, see LN 87.17.

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to take special notice of something, with the implication of concerning oneself
s.g: to take notice of; to consider; to pay attention to; to concern oneself with
s.c: Though the terms ἐπιβλέπω, ἐπεῖδον (ἐφοράω), and ὁράω suggest as a result of their central meanings some measure of visual perception, what is involved in these specific contexts is much more than visual perception. The focus is actually upon intellectual activity and concern.|For another interpretation of ἐπιβλέπω in ⟦Luke 9:38|Luke 9:38⟧, see LN 35.8.

s.d: to provide help, with the implication of having taken special notice of
s.g: to help; to be concerned with; to look upon and help
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπιβλέπω in ⟦Luke 9:38|Luke 9:38⟧, see LN 30.45.

s.dp: Status › Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
s.d: to regard a person as deserving special respect
s.g: to pay special respect to; to look upon as being someone to be honored
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπιβλέπω in ⟦James 2:3|James 2:3⟧, see LN 24.12.

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: a piece of cloth sewed on clothing to repair a hole or tear
s.g: patch
s.c: The statement in ⟦Matthew 9:16|Matthew 9:16⟧ that ‘no one puts a patch of new cloth on an old garment’ seems almost preposterous or incredible in some societies, since people habitually repair old clothing by putting on patches of new cloth, sometimes to the point where it is difficult to determine what was the original fabric. In ⟦Matthew 9:16|Matthew 9:16⟧ the phrase ῥάκους ἀγνάφου, often translated ‘new cloth,’ is literally ‘unshrunken cloth,’ in other words, cloth which has not been washed one or more times and thus has been shrunken in the process. In biblical times there was no technique for preshrinking cloth.

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: a plan for treacherous activity against someone
s.g: plot; plan; scheme

s.d: to marry the childless widow of one’s brother (the so-called levirate marriage; see {S:00502500500000-00502501000000}
s.g: to marry

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › The Earth's Surface
s.d: pertaining to being located on the earth
s.g: on the earth; in the world

s.d: pertaining to human, earthly activity (primarily in contrast with divine activity)
s.g: human; of people

s.d: to happen, with the implication that what happens is different from a previous state{N:001}
s.g: to happen; to occur; to come to be

s.d: to possess more or less definite information about, possibly with a degree of thoroughness or competence
s.g: to know about; to know definitely about; knowledge about

s.d: to come to an understanding as the result of ability to experience and learn{N:001}
s.g: to come to understand; to perceive; to comprehend

s.d: to acquire information, probably in a somewhat more exact or detailed form and perhaps with focus upon what is learned (compare {D:27.2})
s.g: to learn about; to find out about
s.c: ἐπιγινώσκω also occurs in legal contexts referring to careful investigation and interrogation, as in ⟦Acts 22:24|Acts 22:24⟧ and ⟦Acts 23:28|Acts 23:28⟧.

s.d: to identify newly acquired information with what had been previously learned or known
s.g: to recognize

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Acknowledge
s.d: to indicate that one does know
s.g: to acknowledge
s.c: It may also be possible to translate the expression in ⟦1 Corinthians 16:18|1 Corinthians 16:18⟧ as ‘you should give these people due recognition’ in the sense of ‘causing to be recognized’ or ‘causing to be acknowledged.’

s.d: possessing more or less definite information about, possibly with a degree of thoroughness or competence
s.g: knowing about; knowing definitely about; knowledge about
s.c: It is also possible to render ἐπίγνωσις in ⟦Romans 1:28|Romans 1:28⟧ as ‘true knowledge.’ For another interpretation of ἐπίγνωσις as part of an idiom in ⟦Romans 1:28|Romans 1:28⟧, see LN 31.28.

s.d: the content of what is definitely known
s.g: what is known; definite knowledge; full knowledge; knowledge

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to come into knowledge) to acquire information about something, with emphasis upon the process involved
s.g: to learn about; to find out; to come to know
s.c: It is also possible to treat the phrase εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἔρχομαι as meaning ‘to come to know’ in the sense of ‘to come to understand’ (see LN 32.17).

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to come into knowledge) to come to understand the meaning of something, with special emphasis upon the process
s.g: to come to understand; to come to know
s.c: One may also interpret εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἔρχομαι as meaning ‘to come to have knowledge of, to come to know’ (see LN 27.4).

s.d: a brief notice used primarily for identification
s.g: inscription; writing

s.d: to write on a surface
s.g: to write on

s.d: to cause to be seen
s.g: to show

s.d: to demonstrate that something is true
s.g: to show to be true; to prove

s.d: to accept the presence of a person with friendliness{N:001}
s.g: to welcome; to receive; to accept; to have as a guest

s.d: to listen or pay attention to a person, with resulting conformity to what is advised or commanded{N:002}
s.g: to pay attention to and obey

s.d: to dwell more or less permanently in a place which is not one’s own country;  (compare related meanings in {D:11.7}.)
s.g: to sojourn; to live as a foreigner

s.d: to add to, with the implication of some reorganization or rearrangement
s.g: to add to; to introduce something new
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘adding something to a covenant’ would be rendered as ‘to say that one must also do something else to fulfill the covenant.’

s.d: to give, with the implication of motion toward the receiver
s.g: to give to; to deliver to

s.d: to give in to a superior power or force
s.g: to give in to; to surrender; to yield

s.dp: Arrange, Organize › Organize [of events and states]
s.d: to cause matters to be ordered in the correct manner
s.g: to set right; to correct; to put into order

s.d: to go down or to sink down, especially of the sun in relationship to some event or state
s.g: to go down; to go down upon
s.c: In a number of languages it may seem very strange to speak of ‘the sun going down upon one’s anger.’ A more natural and more meaningful equivalent may be ‘do not be angry all day long’ or ‘do not be angry even until sundown.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Gentleness, Mildness
s.d: the quality of gracious forbearing
s.g: gentleness; graciousness; forbearance

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Gentleness, Mildness
s.d: pertaining to being gracious and forbearing
s.g: gentle; gracious; forbearing

s.d: to try to learn the location of something by searching for it (presumably somewhat more emphatic or goal-directed than in the case of {L:ζητέω<SDBG:ζητέω:000000>}[a] ‘to try to learn where something is,’ {D:27.41})
s.g: to seek; to search; to try to find out by looking for

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire, Want, Wish
s.d: to desire to have or experience something, with the probable implication of making an attempt to realize one’s desire{N:001}
s.g: to desire; to want to

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (a derivative involving the base {L:θάνατος<SDBG:θάνατος:000000>}[a] ‘death,’ {D:23.99}) pertaining to having been condemned to death
s.g: doomed to die; sentenced to die
s.c: The phrase ‘like men doomed to die’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘like men who will soon be killed’ or ‘… will soon be executed.’

s.d: placing something on something
s.g: putting on; placing on; laying on

s.d: to greatly desire to do or have something
s.g: to long for; to desire very much

s.d: to strongly desire to have what belongs to someone else and/or to engage in an activity which is morally wrong
s.g: to covet; to lust; evil desires; lust; desire

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπιθυμέω<SDBG:ἐπιθυμέω:000000>}[a] ‘to desire very much,’ {D:25.12}) one who very much desires something, whether good or bad
s.g: one who greatly desires

s.d: greatly desiring to do or have something
s.g: longing for; desire
s.c: The phrase ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα may be regarded as a type of Semitic idiom.

s.d: strongly desiring to have what belongs to someone else and/or to engage in an activity which is morally wrong
s.g: coveting; lust; desire

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Sit
s.d: to sit down upon something
s.g: to sit upon; to mount; to get on
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 21:7|Matthew 21:7⟧ the pronominal form αὐτῶν is ambiguous in reference, for it may refer either to the garments or to the donkey and colt. The closest noun reference is τὰ ἱμάτια ‘the garments,’ but in view of Matthew’s quotation and evident interpretation of the reference to ⟦Zechariah 9:9|Zechariah 9:9⟧, both the donkey and the colt may be the substantive referents, though being seated upon two animals at the same time poses real problems of understanding.

s.d: to use an attribution in speaking of a person
s.g: to call; to name
s.c: It is not always possible to determine from the context whether the act involved is an initial naming of a person or simply calling a person by a particular name. Likewise in the case of attributions or titles, it is not always possible to determine whether it is a matter of giving an attribution or title to a person or simply a matter of speaking of or to a person by means of such an attribution or title. In some instances the giving of a title may be made indirect. For example, in ⟦Matthew 1:23|Matthew 1:23⟧ the statement ‘and they will call his name Emmanuel’ suggests the giving of a title, but the process is stated in terms of how people will speak of this person.

s.d: to call upon someone to do something, normally implying an appeal for aid
s.g: to call upon; to appeal to; to ask for help
s.c: ἐπικαλέομαι also occurs in such expressions as ὅς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου (⟦Acts 2:21|Acts 2:21⟧) ‘whoever calls upon the name of the Lord,’ but the meaning is essentially the same as ‘to call upon the Lord,’ since τὸ ὄνομα ‘the name’ may simply be a metonym for ‘the Lord.’

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judicial Hearing, Inquiry
s.d: to claim one’s legal right to have a case reviewed by a higher tribunal
s.g: to appeal one’s case; to appeal to a higher court
s.c: The second clause in ⟦Acts 26:32|Acts 26:32⟧ may also be rendered in a number of languages as ‘if he had not asked for the Emperor to listen to his case’ or ‘… to judge the accusations against him.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to have someone’s name called upon someone) to be acknowledged as belonging to the one whose name is called upon such an individual
s.g: to be one of (God’s) people; to be the people of
s.c: This interpretation of the expression ἐπικαλέομαι τὸ ὄνομά τινος ἐπί τινα is based upon well attested OT usage, and though it is quite different from traditional interpretations of ⟦Acts 9:14|Acts 9:14⟧ and ⟦Acts 15:17|Acts 15:17⟧, it should be followed as reflecting a more satisfactory and accurate interpretation of the passive form of ἐπικαλέω.

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: that which causes something to be known as or to appear to be other than it really is, thus causing its true nature to be unknown
s.g: means of hiding; pretext; means of covering up the true nature of something

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπικαλύπτω ‘to cover over, to put a covering on,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause sin to be forgiven
s.g: to forgive; to cause forgiveness

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in a place on something
s.g: to be on; to lie on

s.d: to press or push against
s.g: to press against; to push against

s.d: to possess power or sanction
s.g: to be in force; to have power over
s.c: In some languages the concept of ‘being in force’ may be expressed simply as ‘to work’ or ‘to do what they are supposed to do’ or ‘to be in control.’ For another interpretation of ἐπίκειμαι in ⟦Hebrews 9:10|Hebrews 9:10⟧, see LN 13.73.

s.d: to keep on doing something with presumed insistence
s.g: to keep on; to continue insisting; to persist in

s.d: to exist, with the implication of having been established and thus having continuity and purpose
s.g: to exist; to exist for; to be set
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπίκειμαι in ⟦Hebrews 9:10|Hebrews 9:10⟧, see LN 76.17.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Philosophical
s.d: pertaining to the philosophical system of the Greek philosopher Epicurus, who taught that the world is a series of fortuitous combinations of atoms and that the highest good is pleasure
s.g: Epicurean; a follower of Epicurus
s.c: In most instances translators have found it more satisfactory to simply transliterate the terms Ἐπικούρειος and Στοϊκός (LN 11.97), but some supplementary note to identify the teachings of the Epicureans and Stoics is important.

s.d: help, with the possible implication of assistance provided by an ally
s.g: help

s.d: to come to a conclusion in the process of thinking and thus to be in a position to make a decision{N:001}
s.g: to come to a conclusion; to decide; to make up one’s mind
s.c: In some languages the process of ‘deciding’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to come to the end in one’s thinking’ or ‘to choose in one’s mind’ or ‘the mind sees its goal.’

s.d: to take hold of or grasp, with focus upon the goal of the motion
s.g: to take hold of; to grasp
s.c: In a number of languages quite different terms must be employed if one is to take someone by the hand in order to lead him or take someone by the hand in order to rescue him. The difference implied in the presumed force or strength required frequently results in quite different words being used.

s.dp: Control, Rule › Seize, Take into Custody
s.d: to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity
s.g: to seize; to arrest

s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐπιλαμβάνομαι<SDBG:ἐπιλαμβάνομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to grasp,’ {D:18.2}) to learn something about someone, with the purpose of seizing, arresting, or overcoming
s.g: to catch; to trap; to seize; to learn in order to seize

s.d: to assist in supplying what may be needed{N:001}
s.g: to help
s.c: Though the meaning of ‘help’ is possible for ἐπιλαμβάνομαι in ⟦Hebrews 2:16|Hebrews 2:16⟧, the more generally accepted interpretation is ‘to be concerned with’ or ‘to take an interest in’ (see LN 30.42).

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to be concerned about, with the implication of possible help
s.g: to be concerned about; to be concerned for
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπιλαμβάνομαι in ⟦Hebrews 2:16|Hebrews 2:16⟧, see LN 35.1.

s.d: to experience some event or state, often with the implication of something negatively valued{N:003}
s.g: to undergo; to experience
s.c: In the expression in ⟦1 Timothy 6:12|1 Timothy 6:12⟧, ἐπιλαβοῦ no doubt also suggests some activity associated with the state of eternal life.

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Not Remembering, Forgetting
s.d: to not recall information concerning some particular matter
s.g: to forget; to not recall

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Recalling and Responding with Appropriate Action
s.d: to not recall and thus to fail to do something
s.g: to forget to do; to neglect; to overlook

s.d: to speak of a person or object by means of a proper name
s.g: to call; to name

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to choose for a particular purpose
s.g: to choose; to select

s.d: to begin to cease
s.g: to begin to come to the end; to fail; to run out
s.c: In some languages this reference to time in ⟦Hebrews 11:32|Hebrews 11:32⟧ must be shifted to one of space, for example, ‘there is not space enough for me to write about Gideon.’

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Not Remembering, Forgetting
s.d: not recalling information concerning some particular matter
s.g: forgetting; not recalling

s.d: pertaining to the part of a whole which remains or continues, and thus constitutes the rest of the whole{N:001}
s.g: rest; remaining; what remains; other

s.d: to explain the meaning of something, with the implication that the text in question is difficult or complex
s.g: to explain; meaning; explanation
s.c: In ⟦2 Peter 1:20|2 Peter 1:20⟧ ἐπίλυσις clearly involves the interpretation, not the formulation, of a text.

s.d: to explain the meaning of something, with the implication that the text in question is difficult or complex
s.g: to explain; meaning; explanation

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπιλύω ‘to untie, to loose,’ not occurring in the NT) to come to a conclusion concerning a presumably difficult or complex matter
s.g: to resolve (a dispute); to settle (a problem); to come to a decision

s.d: to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge{N:001}
s.g: to witness
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in ⟦Luke 21:13|Luke 21:13⟧ it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: to care for with diligent concern
s.g: to care for; to take care of; to provide whatever is needed

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: to care for with diligent concern
s.g: to care for; to take care of; to provide whatever is needed

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to give proper consideration to some issue or matter
s.g: to think about; to be concerned about; to give attention so as to respond

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπιμελέομαι<SDBG:ἐπιμελέομαι:000001>}[b] ‘to think about,’ {D:30.40}) pertaining to the manner of giving thoughtful concern to an activity
s.g: carefully; thoroughly

s.d: to remain in the same place over a period of time{N:001}
s.g: to remain; to stay

s.d: to continue in an activity or state
s.g: to continue; to remain in; to keep on
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἐπιμένω in ⟦John 8:7|John 8:7⟧ as continuing in a place (see ἐπιμένω, LN 85.55), and therefore one may translate ‘as they stood there.’

s.d: to indicate one’s approval or agreement, sometimes only by nodding
s.g: to agree; to consent

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: that which is intended or purposed as the result of thinking
s.g: intention; purpose

s.dp: Communication › Swear, Put Under Oath, Vow
s.d: to swear that one will do something and then not fulfill the promise
s.g: to forswear; to break an oath; to swear and fail to keep
s.c: See also LN 33.465.

s.dp: Communication › Swear, Put Under Oath, Vow
s.d: to take an oath that something is true, when in reality one knows that it is false
s.g: to swear falsely; to perjure oneself
s.c: In the one occurrence in the NT of ἐπιορκέω (LN 33.464). In either case, it is often necessary to be quite specific about the meaning and to introduce sufficient information into the context so that the specific aspect of either breaking an oath or swearing falsely will be clear.

s.dp: Communication › Swear, Put Under Oath, Vow
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπιορκέω<SDBG:ἐπιορκέω:000001>}[b] ‘to swear falsely,’ {D:33.465}) one who swears falsely
s.g: perjurer

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: pertaining to recurring on a daily basis
s.g: daily; on each day
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἐπιούσιος in ⟦Matthew 6:11|Matthew 6:11⟧ as meaning ‘necessary for existence’ or ‘that which is needed for each day’ or ‘that which is needed for the following day’ or ‘… for the future.’ One reason for the difficulties involved in determining the meaning of ἐπιούσιος is the fact that, as Origen stated, it may very well have been coined by the Gospel writers.|For another interpretation of ἐπιούσιος in ⟦Matthew 6:11|Matthew 6:11⟧, see LN 67.206.

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: pertaining to a day which is the same as the day of a discourse
s.g: today; for today
s.c: For several other meanings of ἐπιούσιος, see LN 67.183.

s.d: to press or push against
s.g: to press against; to push against

s.d: to happen suddenly to, with the connotation of something bad and adverse
s.g: to happen to; to fall upon
s.c: In a number of languages it is difficult to speak of ‘insults happening.’ Therefore, it may be necessary to restructure this expression in ⟦Romans 15:3|Romans 15:3⟧ as ‘they began insulting me in the same way they used to insult you.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to fall on the neck) to show special affection for by throwing one’s arms around a person{N:001}
s.g: to hug; to embrace
s.c: A literal translation of ἐπιπίπτω ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον ‘to fall on someone’s neck’ can be seriously misunderstood. In fact, in some languages it is so close to an expression meaning ‘to kill’ that one should normally avoid any literal rendering. At the same time, it is very important not to employ terms for ‘embrace’ and ‘kiss’ in ⟦Acts 20:37|Acts 20:37⟧ which might suggest improper sexual interests.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπιπλήσσω ‘to strike,’ not occurring in the NT) to express strong disapproval as a type of punishment
s.g: to rebuke; to reproach; to denounce

s.d: to long for something, with the implication of recognizing a lack
s.g: to long for; to deeply desire; deep desire

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: to experience a yearning affection for someone
s.g: to have a great affection for; to have a yearning love for
s.c: The nominal phrase with the English term ‘affection’ can and must be expressed in a number of languages by verb phrases or clauses. In ⟦2 Corinthians 9:14|2 Corinthians 9:14⟧ one may translate ‘they love you very much and will pray for you.’

s.d: longing for something, with the implication of recognizing a lack
s.g: longing for; deep desire

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to yearning affection for someone
s.g: yearningly affectionate; longed for; very dear

s.d: to long for something, with the implication of recognizing a lack
s.g: to long for; to deeply desire; deep desire

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move to or on to, generally with the implication of having arrived
s.g: to come to; to arrive

s.d: to stitch or sew pieces of cloth together
s.g: to sew on; to sew to
s.c: This statement in ⟦Mark 2:21|Mark 2:21⟧ may seem entirely senseless in some societies, since it is a familiar practice to sew new cloth on an old garment; in fact, garments may be so patched that it is difficult to determine what was the original piece of cloth. It may, therefore, be important to have some type of marginal explanation.

s.d: to throw or hurl something upon something else{N:001}
s.g: to throw on; to hurl on

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to throw upon or to cast upon) to cause responsibility for something to be upon someone
s.g: to put responsibility on; to make responsible for
s.c: For another explanation of this expression in ⟦1 Peter 5:7|1 Peter 5:7⟧, taking τὴν μέριμναν ἐπιρίπτω ἐπί as an idiom, see LN 25.250.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to cast cares upon) to stop worrying and to put one’s trust in someone
s.g: to put one’s cares upon; to leave one’s worries to
s.c: For another explanation of this expression in ⟦1 Peter 5:7|1 Peter 5:7⟧, taking only ἐπιρίπτω ἐπί as an idiom, see LN 90.18.

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: pertaining to being well known or outstanding, either because of positive or negative characteristics
s.g: outstanding; famous; notorious; infamous
s.c: In ⟦Romans 16:7|Romans 16:7⟧ the meaning of ‘outstanding’ may be rendered in some instances as ‘well known for being important,’ while ‘notorious’ in ⟦Matthew 27:16|Matthew 27:16⟧ may be rendered in some languages as ‘well known for being bad.’

s.d: any kind of food or nourishment{N:001}
s.g: food
s.c: Almost all languages have at least a few general terms for food, though these may be derived from verbal expressions meaning essentially ‘that which is eaten.’ In some instances a distinction may be made between ‘that which is chewed’ and ‘that which is drunk,’ and it may therefore be important in certain contexts to speak of food in general by a phrase meaning ‘that which is either chewed or drunk.’ If one fails to include both types of food, the reader might interpret a passage such as ⟦Matthew 6:11|Matthew 6:11⟧ as requesting only solid foods.|In the place of a general term or phrase such as ‘that which is eaten’ or ‘that which is consumed,’ some languages generalize the meaning of a particular term. For example, in certain parts of the Orient the term meaning specifically ‘rice’ also refers to ‘food’ in general. In fact, some persons will declare, ‘I have not eaten!’ if they have not had rice as part of a meal. A similar type of meaning has developed in English with respect to ‘bread.’ For example, in rendering ⟦Luke 4:4|Luke 4:4⟧ (οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ‘man shall not live by bread alone’) it would be wrong to employ a strictly literal rendering, since this might mean simply that people should not live on a diet consisting solely of bread. The meaning of ⟦Luke 4:4|Luke 4:4⟧ is, of course, ‘to live means more than merely eating.’

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to choose or select on the basis of having investigated carefully
s.g: to select carefully; to choose after careful investigation

s.d: to go to see a person on the basis of friendship and with helpful intent
s.g: to visit; to go to see
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπισκέπτομαι in ⟦Matthew 25:43|Matthew 25:43⟧, see LN 35.39.

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: to care for or look after, with the implication of continuous responsibility
s.g: to look after; to take care of; to see to
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἐπισκέπτομαι in ⟦Matthew 25:43|Matthew 25:43⟧ as meaning ‘to visit’ (see LN 34.50).

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be present, with the implication of concern{N:001}
s.g: to be present to help; to be on hand to aid

s.d: to come to dwell in a place defined psychologically or spiritually (with the possible implication in some contexts of a temporary arrangement)
s.g: to take up residence; to come to reside; to come to dwell
s.c: In their NT contexts, σκηνόω and ἐπισκηνόω are essentially figurative in meaning, for they deal with spiritual existence and residence rather than human residence or dwelling. In translating one should, in so far as possible, try to preserve this important figurative relationship, since it expresses one of the most significant ways in which spiritual and human existence can be combined. In some languages, however, it may be necessary to employ an expression which means simply ‘to be in’ or ‘to continue with,’ since expressions for ‘living’ or ‘dwelling’ may be based upon terms which are too specific in meaning, for example, ‘to eat from the same pot’ or ‘to enter by the same door.’

s.d: to cause a shadow by interposing something between an object and a source of light
s.g: to cast a shadow upon
s.c: In ⟦Acts 5:15|Acts 5:15⟧ there is a semantic duplication of the element of ‘shadow’ in view of the noun σκιά and the verb ἐπισκιάζω. In ⟦Matthew 17:5|Matthew 17:5⟧ the shining cloud would not produce the same kind of shadow as in the case of ⟦Acts 5:15|Acts 5:15⟧, but it would be interposed between (1) the sun and (2) Jesus and his disciples. In ⟦Matthew 17:5|Matthew 17:5⟧ the shining cloud may thus be more like a covering than a shadow. The reference to this shining cloud in ⟦Matthew 17:5|Matthew 17:5⟧ as the Shekinah of God is discussed in LN 14.49 and LN 14.50.|In ⟦Luke 1:35|Luke 1:35⟧ ἐπισκιάζω is used figuratively in speaking of the agency of the Holy Spirit in causing Mary to conceive: πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέκαὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι the Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.|In a number of languages it is not possible, however, to translate ἐπισκιάζω literally as ‘overshadow.’ It may therefore be necessary to use some such expression as the power of the Most High will come to you or God’s power will come upon you. A strictly literal rendering of ἐπισκιάζω in ⟦Luke 1:35|Luke 1:35⟧ could be interpreted in some languages as being a rather crude reference to sexual intercourse, and this interpretation should be avoided.

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: to care for or look after, with the implication of continuous responsibility
s.g: to look after; to take care of; to see to
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπισκοπέω in ⟦Hebrews 12:15|Hebrews 12:15⟧, see LN 30.46.

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to give careful consideration to something, with the implication of guarding against
s.g: to give careful attention to; to consider carefully; to guard against
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπισκοπέω in ⟦Hebrews 12:15|Hebrews 12:15⟧, see LN 35.39. Some scholars have seen in the occurrence of ἐπισκοπέω in ⟦Hebrews 12:15|Hebrews 12:15⟧ a meaning at least somewhat similar to that which occurs in ἐπισκοπέω ‘to be responsible, to care for’ (LN 53.70).

s.d: to have responsibility for the care of someone, implying a somewhat official responsibility within a congregation
s.g: to minister unto; to be responsible; to care for
s.c: It is possible, however, that ἐπισκοπέω in ⟦1 Peter 5:2|1 Peter 5:2⟧ is not to be understood as designating some official responsibility but merely as a role of helping and serving (see LN 35.39).

s.d: the coming of divine power, either for benefit or judgment
s.g: coming; visitation
s.c: In ⟦1 Peter 2:12|1 Peter 2:12⟧ the reference may be to God’s coming to rule or his coming in judgment.

s.d: a religious role involving both service and leadership
s.g: office; position; ministry as church leader
s.c: See discussion at LN 53.71. For a more probable interpretation of ἐπισκοπή in ⟦Acts 1:20|Acts 1:20⟧, see LN 35.40.

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπισκοπέω<SDBG:ἐπισκοπέω:000000>}[a] ‘to take care of,’ {D:35.39}) the position of one who has responsibility for the care of someone
s.g: position of responsibility; position of oversight
s.c: Though in some contexts ἐπισκοπή has been regarded traditionally as a position of authority, in reality the focus is upon the responsibility for caring for others, and in the context of ⟦Acts 1:20|Acts 1:20⟧ the reference is clearly to the responsibility for caring for the church (see LN 53.69).

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: one who has the responsibility of caring for spiritual concerns
s.g: one responsible for; one who cares for; guardian; keeper
s.c: In ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧ ἐπίσκοπος is applied to Christ, and it no doubt shares certain of the meanings associated with ἐπίσκοπος in LN 53.71, but the focus in ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧ is not upon leadership but upon the role of caring for the believers.

s.d: one who serves as a leader in a church
s.g: church leader
s.c: For ἐπίσκοπος in ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧, see LN 35.43.|In translating ἐπισκοπή (LN 53.69), ἐπισκοπέω (LN 53.70), or ἐπίσκοπος, it is important to try to combine the concepts of both service and leadership, in other words, the responsibility of caring for the needs of a congregation as well as directing the activities of the membership. In some translations an equivalent may be ‘helper’ and ‘leader.’

s.d: (a technical and medical term) to pull the foreskin over the end of the penis as a means of concealing former circumcision
s.g: to conceal circumcision; to extend the foreskin
s.c: A literal and descriptive rendering of ἐπισπάομαι could prove to be quite vulgar in some languages. Furthermore, such a practice might seem to be medically impossible or absurd, so that in general, translators have used some such expression as ‘do not conceal the circumcision’ or ‘do not change the circumcision to appear like uncircumcision,’ but often some additional marginal note is required if people are to understand satisfactorily what is involved.

s.d: to possess information about, with the implication of an understanding of the significance of such information{N:001}
s.g: to know

s.d: to have or gain insight, with focus upon the process
s.g: to understand; to be aware of; to really know

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: a state of prolonged concern and anxiety
s.g: pressure; concern; burden
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐπίστασις in ⟦2 Corinthians 11:28|2 Corinthians 11:28⟧, see LN 35.42.

s.d: rising up in open defiance of authority, with the presumed intention to overthrow it or to act in complete opposition to its demands{N:001}
s.g: revolt; insurrection; rebellion
s.c: It is also possible that ἀποστασία differs slightly in meaning from ἐπίστασις by virtue of the differences in prefixal formation, but there is insufficient contextual evidence to support such a view.

s.dp: Help, Care For › Care For, Take Care Of
s.d: responsibility for oversight based upon authority
s.g: responsibility for; concern for; care of
s.c: Though one might regard ἐπίστασις as meaning only the position of authority, nevertheless this authority is expressed in terms of the oversight and care of others. In a sense the meaning of ἐπίστασις in ⟦2 Corinthians 11:28|2 Corinthians 11:28⟧ is defined by the following appositional phrase, ἡ μέριμνα πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν ‘concern for all the churches.’ For another interpretation of ἐπίστασις in ⟦2 Corinthians 11:28|2 Corinthians 11:28⟧, see LN 25.239.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a person of high status, particularly in view of a role of leadership
s.g: leader; master

s.d: communicate with someone by means of a letter
s.g: to write a letter; to send a letter to

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπίσταμαι<SDBG:ἐπίσταμαι:000001>}[b] ‘to understand,’ {D:32.3}) pertaining to being able to understand and evaluate
s.g: intelligent; insightful; understanding

s.d: to cause someone to become stronger in the sense of more firm and unchanging in attitude or belief
s.g: to strengthen; to make more firm

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: an object containing writing addressed to one or more persons
s.g: letter (normally written on papyrus)
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to try to distinguish between a letter as an object and a letter as content or message. In ⟦Acts 23:33|Acts 23:33⟧ the focus seems to be upon the letter as an object, not necessarily upon the contents of the document. In most contexts, however, it is impossible to distinguish between a letter as a material object and a letter as a message (see LN 33.48).

s.d: a written communication, usually from one person to one or more persons{N:001}
s.g: letter
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἐπιστολή in ⟦Acts 23:25|Acts 23:25⟧ not as a content or message, but as an object (see LN 6.63)

s.d: to cause someone to stop talking
s.g: to silence; to keep someone from speaking

s.d: to return to a point or area where one has been before, with probable emphasis on turning about
s.g: to return to; to go back to; to turn around

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to change one’s belief, with focus upon that to which one turns
s.g: to turn to; to come to believe; to come to accept
s.c: In analyzing the meaning of στρέφω, ἐπιστρέφω, and ἐπιστροφή in such passages as ⟦Galatians 4:9|Galatians 4:9⟧ and ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧, it is difficult to determine the extent to which belief or behavior is primarily in focus. In the case of ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧, one could certainly argue that the emphasis is upon the interpersonal relationship. It is therefore essential in rendering these terms not to narrow the meaning too much, for in this way one would certainly do violence to certain crucial semantic features.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to cause a person to change belief, with focus upon that to which one turns
s.g: to cause to change belief; to cause to turn to

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: to change one’s manner of life in a particular direction, with the implication of turning back to God
s.g: to change one’s ways; to turn to God; repentance
s.c: In a number of languages it is not sufficient to simply translate ‘to change one’s manner of life,’ for this could either be neutral or even suggest a change for the worse. Therefore, it may be necessary in a number of instances to translate ‘to change one’s way of living as God would want’ or ‘to change and live like God would want one to live.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to turn hearts to) to cause a change of attitude in a positive and acceptable direction
s.g: to make well-disposed toward; to make friendly toward; to cause to become acceptable

s.d: to turn around to or toward
s.g: to turn around; to turn toward

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: changing one’s belief, with focus upon that to which one turns
s.g: turning to; coming to believe; acceptance; conversion
s.c: In analyzing the meaning of στρέφω, ἐπιστρέφω, and ἐπιστροφή in such passages as ⟦Acts 15:3|Acts 15:3⟧, it is difficult to determine the extent to which belief or behavior is primarily in focus. In the case of ⟦1 Peter 2:25|1 Peter 2:25⟧, one could certainly argue that the emphasis is upon the interpersonal relationship. It is therefore essential in rendering these terms not to narrow the meaning too much, for in this way one would certainly do violence to certain crucial semantic features.|For another interpretation of ἐπιστροφή in ⟦Acts 15:3|Acts 15:3⟧, see LN 41.51.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: change in one’s manner of life in a particular direction, with the implication of turning back to God
s.g: changing of one’s ways; turning to God; repentance
s.c: In a number of languages it is not sufficient to simply translate ‘to change one’s manner of life,’ for this could either be neutral or even suggest a change for the worse. Therefore, it may be necessary in a number of instances to translate ‘to change one’s way of living as God would want’ or ‘to change and live like God would want one to live.’|For a different interpretation of ἐπιστροφή in ⟦Acts 15:3|Acts 15:3⟧, see LN 31.60.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to cause to come together to, toward, or at a particular location
s.g: to cause to come together; to gather together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to come or gather together to, toward, or at a particular location
s.g: to gather (at); to come together (to)

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: causing to come together to, toward, or at a particular location
s.g: causing to come together; gathering together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
